title: Understanding the Problem
text: The problem involves comparing two ridge regression models, \( \hat{\theta}_A \) and \( \hat{\theta}_B \), where the difference lies in whether the intercept term is regularized. We need to determine if \( \hat{\theta}_A $$=$$ \hat{\theta}_B \) when using a mean-centered design matrix.

title: Mean-Centering Effect
text: Mean-centering the design matrix \( \tilde{\mathbb{X}} \) implies that all columns except the intercept have a mean of zero. This affects the regularization of the intercept term.

title: Impact of Regularizing the Intercept
text: When the design matrix is mean-centered, the intercept term does not affect the mean of the predictors. Therefore, regularizing the intercept term has no impact on the solution.

title: Conclusion
text: Given that mean-centering nullifies the effect of regularizing the intercept, what can we conclude about \( \hat{\theta}_A \) and \( \hat{\theta}_B \)?
